summary: Petition under section 79(1)(b) and 79 (1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 for claiming compensation on account of event pertaining to change in law as per the terms of Power Purchase Agreements dated 13.6.2013 (PPAs) executed between the Petitioner and the Respondents. 5. In the present petition, the Petitioner has sought compensation on account of the events of change in law affecting the power project in order to restore the Petitioner to the same economic position as if the events have not occurred in terms of the KSEB PPA. 7. The Petitioner has sought compensation for Change in Law events during the Operating period on account of the following events which have impacted the cost and revenue of supply of power from the power project to the procure: c) Direct the Respondent to continue to make payments accrued in favour of the Petitioner on account of Change in Law events mentioned in prayer (A), post 31.08.2016, in terms of the protocol/ formula envisaged in Annexure CC of the Petition, till the validity of the PPAs dated 13.06.2013; and d) Pass such other and further order or orders as this Hon‟ble Commission deems appropriate under the facts and circumstances of the present case.” (b) Article 15.18 qua "Taxes and Duties" and Article 10 qua "Change-inLaw" of the PPA dated 13.6.2013 are mutually exclusive. While the Petitioner is agreeable to the payment of taxes, cess/ levy as mandated under Article 15.18, the stipulations contained in Article 10 still mandates KSEB to compensate the Petitioner and restore it to the position seven days prior to the bid submission date, which otherwise would mar the financial interests of the Petitioner due to change in law events. The Petitioner undertakes to abide by the terms of Article 15.18 which however is a charge to be paid to the Government but the said charge can under no circumstance be construed to override the bilateral terms of Article 10 which require the procurer to compensate the generator and offset an adverse economic impact on account of change in law events. (a) The claims made by the Petitioner include various items which are not in pursuance to any statutory levy or tax applicable for the supply of power, as envisaged in Article 10.1.1 to be a change in law. Such claims cannot be considered as Change in Law. (g) The Petitioner had the option of quoting escalable charges and participated in the bid being aware of the escalation. It is not open to the Petitioner to now claim that the escalation index mechanism is not adequate. The Petitioner has not challenged the escalation index. Further, the Petitioner had accepted the bid terms and conditions and knowingly participated in the bidding process. (a) Whether the Commission has the jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute between the Petitioner and the Respondent with regard to change in law event? # **Issue No. 1: Whether the Commission has the jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute between the Petitioner and the Respondent with regard to Change in law event?** 25. The claim of the Petitioner in the present petition pertains to Change in law events related to the PPA dated 13.6.2013. The cut-off date for consideration of any claim for change in law, namely 7 days before the bid deadline, is 4.3.2013. Article 10.4 of the PPA between KSEB and the Seller (PTC India Ltd.) envisages for notification of Change in Law events, respectively to the Procurer. Article 10.4 of the KSEB PPA is extracted as under: 27. The claims of the Petitioner are with respect to events under Change in Law under Article 10 of the PPA. Article 10 of the PPA between the Petitioner/ PTC and KSEB deals with events of Change in Law during the operating period and is extracted for reference as under: parties arising out of claim made by any party for any change in or determination of In the event that the parties are unable to resolve any dispute, controversy or claim relating to or arising under this agreement or in the determination of tariff and other matters related to tariff, which are falling under the provisions of Electricity Act 2003, such Disputes shall be submitted to adjudication by the Appropriate Commission. Appeal against the decisions of the Appropriate Commission shall be made only as per the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003, as amended from time to time.” 28. A combined reading of the above provisions reveals the events broadly covered under Change in Law and that this Commission has the jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the dispute between the Petitioner and KSEB. These events are: 29. In the light of above and in view of the broad principles discussed above, we proceed to deal with the claims of the Petitioner under Change in Law during the Operating Period. 66. We have considered the submissions of the parties. It is noted that the Petitioner has not submitted documents in support of its claim in the absence of which no view can be taken as regards the admissibility under Change in Law. 69. We have considered the submissions of the parties. It is noted that the Petitioner has not submitted required documents in support of its claim including the State whose VAT is applicable in this case. Therefore, we are not inclined to grant any relief at this stage in the absence of statutory/required documents. Therefore, the Petitioner claim on this aspect is rejected. However, the Petitioner is granted liberty to approach the Commission for appropriate relief along with all required documents. the Petitioner and Coal India Limited. The Petitioner has already quoted an escalable component of energy charges and shall be compensated for any revision in base price of coal through Escalation Index. Therefore, the Petitioner was expected to take into account the possible revision in these charges while quoting the bid. Accordingly, the claim of the Petitioner on this account is disallowed.
title: Petition under section 79(1)(b) and 79 (1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 for claiming compensation on account of event pertaining to change in law as per the terms of Power Purchase Agreements dated 13.6.2013 (PPAs) executed between the Petitioner and the Respondents Bharat Aluminium Company Limited.
